sec: Progression, vertical transmission, treatment in pregnancy, newborn care, post-exposure prophylaxis, vaccine prophylaxis

items.q: Fill up (Progression, Part 2): the printed chain runs Acute hepatitis → ______ → Cirrhosis, and cirrhosis ends in the two drawn end-points ______.
opts: Chronic hepatitis; hepatocellular carcinoma and liver failure
Chronic hepatitis; portal hypertension and variceal bleed
Fulminant hepatitis; hepatocellular carcinoma and liver failure
Chronic hepatitis; cholangiocarcinoma and portal vein thrombosis
items.exp: 'Acute Hepatitis → Chronic Hepatitis → Cirrhosis', with the cirrhosis box arrowed to 'HCC' and 'Liver failure'. (Book p1039)

items.q: In the p1039 progression diagram, cirrhosis arrows into two end-points. Which of these is NOT one of them?
items.exp: Only 'HCC' and 'Liver failure' are drawn from the cirrhosis box. (Book p1039)

items.q: Judge the Part-2 progression diagram: I Cirrhosis is drawn downstream of chronic hepatitis. II Recovery is drawn as an end-point of cirrhosis.
items.exp: Acute → chronic hepatitis → cirrhosis → HCC / liver failure; no recovery branch is drawn from cirrhosis. (Book p1039)

items.q: Under 'Transmission (Acute)' the page lists three routes. Which one is NOT among them?
items.exp: The printed arms are Sexual, Per-cutaneous and Blood transfusion; vertical transmission is handled in its own block below. (Book p1039)

items.q: How is vertical transmission described in this block?
items.exp: 'Transmission : vertical (mother to child).' (Book p1039)

items.q: Vertical transmission block — match — 1) HBeAg positive mother 2) HBeAg negative mother … A) 10% chances B) 90% chances
items.exp: Below HBeAg the block prints '90% chances' and '10% chances' for transmission to the child. (Book p1039)

items.q: Fill up: 'Time of development : ______ trimester (______)'.
items.exp: 'Time of development : 3rd trimester (maximum)'. (Book p1039)

items.q: At what gestation does the pregnancy block advise the check-up?
items.exp: 'Treatment in Pregnancy : At 28 - 30 week → check-up'. (Book p1039)

items.q: Antenatal HBV DNA comes back above the printed cut-off. What is the next printed step and the threshold used?
opts: Start treatment once HBV DNA exceeds 20,000
Start treatment only after delivery, whatever the HBV DNA
Start treatment once HBV DNA exceeds 2,000
Give HBIG to the mother immediately, whatever the HBV DNA
items.exp: 'check-up → HBV DNA → > 20,000 → Start treatment'. (Book p1039)

items.q: Judge the pregnancy block: I The antenatal check-up with HBV DNA is timed at 28–30 weeks. II Treatment is started when HBV DNA crosses 20,000.
items.exp: Both statements reproduce the printed block: check-up at 28–30 weeks, and 'Start treatment' after HBV DNA > 20,000. (Book p1039)

items.q: Fill up (Child after birth): immunoglobulin — HBIg (______ ml); vaccine — ______, with the first dose within ______ hours.
items.exp: 'Child After birth : Immunoglobulin : HBIg (0.5 ml). Vaccine : 0,1,6 / 0,1,6 (1st dose within 12 hours)'. (Book p1039)

items.q: Post-exposure prophylaxis after a needlestick from an HBV-positive patient — what risk figure is printed?
items.exp: 'Needle prick : HBV +ve patient (6-30% chances) → Check for Anti HBs levels'. (Book p1039)

items.q: Needlestick algorithm — match the anti-HBs level to the printed action — 1) > 100 2) 10 – 100 … A) 1 booster to be given B) No need for Ig / vaccine
items.exp: '> 100 : No need for Ig/vaccine'; '10-100 : 1 booster to be given'. (Book p1039)

items.q: After a needlestick from an HBV-positive source, what is the investigation the page asks for before deciding on prophylaxis?
opts: Check anti-HBc IgM in the recipient
items.exp: 'Check for Anti HBs levels' is the branch point of the algorithm. (Book p1039)

items.q: Fill up (Sexual-contact exposure): HBIG ______ mL/kg given within ______ days.
items.exp: 'Sexual contact : HBIg : 0.06 mL/kg within 14 days'. (Book p1039)

items.q: Fill up (Percutaneous / transmucosal exposure): HBIG ______ mL/kg given within ______ hours.
items.exp: 'Percutaneous/transmucosal : HBIg : 0.06 ml/kg within 24 hours'. (Book p1039)

items.q: Compare the two post-exposure columns: I Sexual contact allows HBIG up to 14 days. II Percutaneous/transmucosal exposure allows HBIG only up to 24 hours.
items.exp: Sexual contact: 'within 14 days'; percutaneous/transmucosal: 'within 24 hours'. (Book p1039)

items.q: Post-exposure vaccination — match — 1) Sexual contact 2) Percutaneous/transmucosal … A) Vaccine 0,1,6 months, 1st dose within 1 week B) Vaccine 0,1,6 months, 1st dose within 1 week — identical in both
items.exp: Both columns print 'Vaccine : 0,1,6 / 0,1,6 months' and '1st dose within 1 week'. (Book p1039)

items.q: Vaccine prophylaxis — match — 1) General population 2) In CKD patient … A) Schedule 0,1,2,6 months; 40 μg / 1 ml; both deltoid (double dose) B) Schedule 0,1,6 months; 20 μg / 0.5 ml; deltoid
items.exp: General population: 0,1,6 months, 20 μg / 0.5 ml, deltoid. CKD: 0,1,2,6 months, 40 μg / 1 ml, both deltoid (double dose). (Book p1039)

items.q: What route is printed for hepatitis B vaccine prophylaxis in both the general population and the CKD patient?
items.exp: 'Route : im' in both columns. (Book p1039)

items.q: Which of these is NOT printed for the CKD vaccination schedule?
items.exp: The CKD column prints 0,1,2,6 months, 40 μg / 1 ml and 'Both Deltoid (double dose)'. (Book p1039)
